definition: Penalising divergence from a reference policy during reinforcement learning, present in nearly every archived training recipe at coefficients typically around 0.001. Across 6 sources it appears mostly as machinery rather than as a subject, and the informative uses are diagnostic. Its trajectory is read as evidence: one source reports KL from the frozen model rising steadily as an argument against representational collapse while noting this does not rule out subtler coupling, and another finds the strictest reward tolerance producing the lowest KL trajectory -- meaning the policy never left its initialisation, which is how a sparse reward fails silently. One source names it as part of the trust-region approximation that sits outside its own theorems, so results proven for an unclipped unregularised objective do not transfer to the deployed method. And it is the standard remedy proposed for general-capability forgetting during reasoning training, though the archive's evidence on that is that the damage is often localised to one language or one benchmark rather than diffuse, which a single divergence penalty is poorly shaped to address.

evidence.note: Shows that supervised fine-tuning can install a triggered backdoor whose visible reasoning stays clean, correct and topically benign while the final answer is attacker-chosen — leaving CoT-only monitors at chance (AUC 0.44-0.55) and recovering detection only when the monitor is shown the answer alongside the trace (0.76-1.00).
evidence.title: Evading Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Through Model Poisoning

evidence.note: Scores each reasoning step of a translation by how much appending it raises a frozen reference model's teacher-forced likelihood of the gold translation, and adds that as a dense per-step reward on top of sequence-level quality — after first establishing that explicit reasoning helps long and hard inputs while drifting on terminology and style.
evidence.title: PAMT: Process-Aligned Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Domain Machine Translation

evidence.note: Trains a multimodal agent to orchestrate twelve video-analysis tools for anomaly detection with GRPO under a dual reward that combines exact-match rule checks with an LLM judge scoring logicality, relevance and completeness, and releases the benchmark it is evaluated on.
evidence.title: VTO: Visual Tool Orchestration for Video Anomaly Detection

evidence.note: Gives the teacher in on-policy self-distillation access to each completed student rollout and its verified outcome, adapting it to preserve behaviour on successes and redirect failures toward verified success, while the student keeps a prefix-only interface it can actually deploy.
evidence.title: PAST: Privileged Adaptation from Complete Student Trajectories for On-Policy Self-Distillation

evidence.note: Trains an open-weight model with GRPO against a safety-gated LLM-as-a-judge rubric for financial advice, then audits the result with a judge-independent causal estimator on logged outcomes -- and finds the two evaluations rank the other systems differently, with the untrained base model last on the rubric and second on the audit.
evidence.title: GRPO for Financial Advice Generation: Outperforming Commercial LLMs under CATE Evaluation

evidence.note: Confirms that prolonged RLVR makes models forget foundational skills, and counters it with experience replay whose objective weights adapt online to convergence and instability signals.
evidence.title: Beyond Reasoning Gains: Mitigating General-Capability Forgetting in Large Reasoning Models

name: KL regularization
